newsitem.title: USA: Fruit of the Loom cuts 1,480 jobs in Kentucky.
newsitem.headline: Fruit of the Loom cuts 1,480 jobs in Kentucky.

text.p: Fruit of the Loom Inc. said Thursday it will eliminate 1,480 sewing and garment assembly jobs at its Campbellsville, Ky., textile facility due to intense competition in the apparel industry.
The Chicago-based apparel manufacturer said it expects to take a pretax charge of between $14 million to $22 million in the second half of the year to cover severance and downsizing costs.
Fruit of the Loom, whose brands include Fruit of the Loom and BVD, said its Campbellsville workers will be offered 1,000 new jobs created throughout the company recently.
At the same time, the company will create 150 jobs at the facility in its knitting, dying and bleaching operation, spokesman Mark Steinkrauss said.

"We are very efficient. We are the low cost producer. But in sewing, the wage disparity is wide from other locations offshore," Steinkrauss said in a telephone interview from the company's central Kentucky plant.
He said the company gave employees notice today that the jobs cuts will likely take effect over the next 60 days.
"These are great workers but these are global pressures and we have to stay competitive," he said. "Other manufacturers have gone offshore. We have tried to stay in the U.S."
Fruit of the Loom, which employs 36,000 people worldwide, has moved some jobs overseas in the past five years and has facilities in the Caribbean, Mexico and Central America.

Last month, Fruit of the Loom reported its 1997 second-quarter earnings fell to $23.2 million, or 31 cents a share, from $47.8 million, or 63 cents a share, a year earlier. Sales declined to $640.7 million from $732.2 million in the 1996 second quarter.
At that time, the company said it was disappointed with the results and would take steps to increase revenue, reduce costs and improve profitability.
Shares of Fruit of the Loom fell 25 cents to close at $26.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
